relationship.statement: For small swings, a pendulum's period depends only on its length and gravity, not on the bob's mass. Changing the release angle changes the swing width and peak speed, and slightly increases the period at large angles.
assumptions: The bob is modeled as a point mass on a massless, rigid rod.
Pivot friction and air resistance are neglected.
Gravity is held fixed at Earth's surface (9.81 m/s^2).

quantities.label: Length
quantities.meaning: Distance from the pivot point to the center of the bob

quantities.label: Bob mass
quantities.meaning: Mass of the hanging pendulum bob

quantities.label: Release angle
quantities.meaning: Starting angle from vertical when the bob is released

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Downward gravitational acceleration acting on the bob

quantities.label: Period
quantities.meaning: Time required for one complete back-and-forth swing

quantities.label: Frequency
quantities.meaning: Number of full swings completed each second

quantities.label: Max speed
quantities.meaning: Peak speed of the bob as it passes the lowest point

quantities.label: Angle
quantities.meaning: Current angle of the pendulum from vertical over time

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { var L = inputs.length; var g = 9.81; var theta0 = 20 * Math.PI / 180; var period = 2 * Math.PI * Math.sqrt(L / g); var frequency = 1 / period; var maxSpeed = Math.sqrt(2 * g * L * (1 - Math.cos(theta0))); var omega = 2 * Math.PI / period; var theta = theta0 * Math.cos(omega * t); var dTheta = -theta0 * omega * Math.sin(omega * t); var angle = theta * 180 / Math.PI; var bobX = 0.8 + L * Math.sin(theta); var bobY = -L * Math.cos(theta); var vx = L * Math.cos(theta) * dTheta; var vy = L * Math.sin(theta) * dTheta; var velTipX = bobX + 0.3 * vx; var velTipY = bobY + 0.3 * vy; var refL = 1.0; var refPeriod = 2 * Math.PI * Math.sqrt(refL / g); var refOmega = 2 * Math.PI / refPeriod; var refTheta = theta0 * Math.cos(refOmega * t); var refAngle = refTheta * 180 / Math.PI; var refX = -0.8 + refL * Math.sin(refTheta); var refY = -refL * Math.cos(refTheta); return { period: period, frequency: frequency, maxSpeed: maxSpeed, angle: angle, bobX: bobX, bobY: bobY, velTipX: velTipX, velTipY: velTipY, refAngle: refAngle, refX: refX, refY: refY, isShorter: L < 0.99, isEqualRef: Math.abs(L - 1.0) <= 0.01, isLonger: L > 1.01 }; }

lesson.title: How does rod length change a pendulum swing?
lesson.description: Compare an adjustable pendulum with a fixed 1 m reference swinging from 20 degrees. Change the length to watch how period, frequency, and speed respond.
lesson.instructions: Drag the Length slider between 0.4 m and 2.0 m, and use play or scrub to compare both swings and their angle curves over 5 seconds.
lesson.goal: With mass, release angle, and gravity held fixed, increasing pendulum length increases the period and peak speed while decreasing frequency.
